Pathogenic variants in OCRL lead to impaired inositol phosphate metabolism, causing renal tubulopathy in Dent disease type 2. Pathogenic variants in PLCB3 impair lysosomal function, leading to corneal dystrophy and spondylometaphyseal dysplasia in the second disease. The convergence is on the shared pathways of inositol phosphate metabolism and lysosomal function, which are intertwined.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of any overlap in the functional consequences of OCRL and PLCB3 mutations on cellular pathways related to lipid or phosphate metabolism, or lysosomal trafficking, would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: Common variants in OCRL or PLCB3 (AF > 0.01) in gnomAD that do not segregate with either disease.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared downstream pathways of inositol phosphate metabolism and lysosomal function affected by mutations in OCRL and PLCB3 could reveal novel therapeutic targets for both Dent disease type 2 and spondylometaphyseal dysplasia with corneal dystrophy, potentially through modulating these common pathways.
